channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Nepal Urges Tourists Not to Abandon Himalayas After Floods
item.description: Nepal urged international travelers not to abandon the Himalayas, declaring the country open for tourism as it continues to assess the human and economic toll from catastrophic floods that killed hundreds and left thousands missing.
item.dc:creator: Swati Pandey

item.title: Trump’s Energy Chief Says Venezuela Poised to Double Oil Output
item.description: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said companies are on the cusp of signing a series of deals that will put Venezuela on pace to rapidly expand its output of crude.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter

item.title: Hong Kong Activist Joshua Wong Pleads Guilty to Collusion
item.description: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong pleaded guilty to foreign collusion on Wednesday, media outlets reported, his second conviction under a Beijing-imposed security law that’s transformed the financial hub.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan

item.title: Octogenarian Markey Fends Off Massachusetts Senate Challenge
item.description: Massachusetts Senator Ed Markey won the state’s Democratic primary on Tuesday, NBC and AP projected, beating back a challenge from a congressman who argued he was too old to continue serving in the chamber.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ryan

item.title: House Bill Funds the Govt. Through Election Day
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Brad Sherman (D-CA) says oil markets predict the US and Iran will return to diplomacy, though he is uncertain how the conflict ultimately ends. Rep. Chip Roy (R-TX) says he opposed the continuing resolution after the Senate added provisions he disagreed with, arguing Congress should instead focus on appropriations bills and spending restraint. Chris Sununu, President and CEO of Airlines for America and former Republican Governor of New Hampshire, says high jet fuel prices are “crushing” the airline industry even as travel demand remains strong. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Taps Hung Cao for Navy Secretary Amid Pentagon Turmoil
item.description: President Donald Trump is nominating acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao for the position on a permanent basis, looking to fill a vacancy in the military’s top leadership at a time when the Iran war has prompted concerns over the impact on personnel and readiness.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey

item.title: Sununu: High Jet Fuel Prices Are Crushing Airline Industry
item.description: Chris Sununu, President and CEO of Airlines for America and former Republican Governor of New Hampshire, says high jet fuel prices are “crushing” the airline industry even as travel demand remains strong. Sununu says airlines are absorbing much of the higher fuel costs and expects that pressure to persist as the Iran conflict drags on. Sununu says the continuing resolution only kicks the can down the road and warns another government shutdown could significantly impact airlines. Sununu says Congress is “not doing their job,” arguing lawmakers are failing to address major fiscal and spending issues. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK Middle Classes Face Tax Hit to Fund Spending, Analysis Finds
item.description: Britain’s middle class would likely need to face higher taxes to fund a bigger state, according to research by the left-leaning Resolution Foundation showing they are squeezed less than international peers.
item.dc:creator: Tom Rees

item.title: Rep. Roy: Congress Must Go Further On Spending Restraints
item.description: Rep. Chip Roy (R-TX) says he opposed the continuing resolution after the Senate added provisions he disagreed with, arguing Congress should instead focus on appropriations bills and spending restraint. He says Republicans need to make tough fiscal decisions to address mounting deficits and deliver fiscal responsibility. Rep. Roy, a former federal prosecutor, says widespread use of Flock cameras raises concerns about government surveillance and argues massive data collection and sharing “has to stop.” He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Duppler: Bessent's AI Outlook Is Optimistic, But Plausible
item.description: Mattie Duppler, Senior Fellow for Fiscal Policy at the National Taxpayers Union and Founder and President of Forward Strategies, discusses Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's closing remarks at the G20 in Ashville. Duppler calls Bessent's expectation for a major AI-driven productivity shift within six months "very optimistic," but says the rapid pace of technological change means it cannot be ruled out. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Palantir’s Karp Will Back Startup by Ex-Ukraine Defense Chief
item.description: Alex Karp, Palantir Technologies Inc.’s chief executive officer, is set to become the first major investor in a defense technology company proposed by Ukraine’s former defense minister as the country continues to battle invading Russian forces.
item.dc:creator: Sonya Dymova

item.title: Trump Pressures Squeezed Refiners to Ease Pump Prices
item.description: President Donald Trump pressed US oil refiners to boost domestic production of gasoline and diesel during a closed-door meeting Tuesday, as he contends with high prices and mounting cost-of-living concerns before November’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Elizabeth Elkin

item.title: Rep. Sherman: Oil Markets Predict Return To Iran Diplomacy
item.description: Rep. Brad Sherman (D-CA) says oil markets predict the US and Iran will return to diplomacy, though he is uncertain how the conflict ultimately ends. Rep. Sherman says he supports tougher sanctions on Russia in principle but wants to review changes to the Senate-passed bill, citing concerns about giving President Trump additional tariff authority. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Daniel Lubetzky Launches ‘Build or Break’ Podcast
item.description: Daniel Lubetzky discusses his new podcast, "Build or Break," set to launch Thursday, and explains that the show will explore the setbacks behind success. He says conversations with entrepreneurs, inventors, filmmakers, and humanitarians revealed a common pattern: successful people do fail, but they do not fall apart. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: California Lawmakers Adjourn Without Voting on Wildfire Bill
item.description: The California Assembly adjourned without passing a revamp of the state’s wildfire response, sending up shares in two key power utilities, PG&E Corp. and Edison International.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Oxford and Michelle Ma

item.title: US-Iran Conflict Intensifies as Trump Downplays Desire for Deal
item.description: The conflict between the US and Iran escalated sharply, with American forces carrying out a fresh wave of strikes and Iran saying it had retaliated.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan, Grant Smith and Eltaf Najafizada

item.title: Xi Returns to Egypt After a Decade That Altered Middle East
item.description: When Chinese President Xi Jinping visits Cairo this week, he’ll find plenty has changed in Egypt and the region since his last trip to the Middle East’s most populous nation a decade ago.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: US, Allies Pledge Aid to Pacific For Fuel, Ports, Drug Control
item.description: The US, Australia and New Zealand have pledged hundreds of millions of dollars in aid for the Pacific region to build up infrastructure, secure fuel and help stop a surge of drugs, ramping up support in a region increasingly contested with China.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: China Removes Tax Exemption on Foreigners’ Dividend Incomes
item.description: China has ended a decadeslong exemption on the individual income tax paid by foreign-invested firms on some dividend payments, the latest in a series of sweeping changes to the country’s tax system.
item.dc:creator: Trista Xinyi Luo

item.title: Brazil Election: Data Centers That Are Hated in US Win Support in Brazil
item.description: Data centers have become politically toxic in the US midterm campaign. Not in Brazil’s presidential race.
item.dc:creator: Peter Millard and Daniel Carvalho
